report.raw: {"schema_version":"m0-report-v2","assessment_status":"completed","conclusion":"supported","summary":"Checkout is firing CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh because the payment service is rejecting card charges with an application-level error thrown inside payment itself: 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. app.loyalty.level=gold' (thrown at payment's /usr/src/app/charge.js:37). Checkout propagates that as gRPC status 13 INTERNAL on oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, and frontend/frontend-proxy/load-generator observe HTTP 500. In the hour ending 2026-11-03T19:23:13Z, 58.97 of checkout's PlaceOrder spans carried STATUS_CODE_ERROR versus 41.68 UNSET (~59%), exactly mirroring the 58.97 errors on checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge client spans and payment's own 57.95 errored grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge server spans. The 5-minute PlaceOrder error ratio was 1.0 at 19:17:13 and 19:18:13, which reproduces the alert annotation's '100% over the last 5 minutes'; the ratio then fell to 0.5/0.25 and to 0 at 19:21:13-19:22:13, so the firing reflects very low, bursty PlaceOrder volume. A comparable 24h baseline shows zero PlaceOrder error spans for ~10 consecutive hours (2026-11-02T20:23Z through 2026-11-03T11:53Z), with errors first appearing around 12:23Z and escalating. Nothing in the evidence shows a pod restart or redeploy of payment or checkout (same pod UIDs and same image digests for 24h), and every other checkout dependency (cart, product-catalog, currency, shipping) had zero error spans; the deepest supported cause is payment's own charge-rejection logic, and what turned it on is not observable with the available sources.","claims":[{"kind":"fact","text":"In the 61 minutes ending 2026-11-03T19:23:13Z, checkout's oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder spans split into 58.97 STATUS_CODE_ERROR and 41.68 STATUS_CODE_UNSET, and checkout's client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge had the identical counts (58.97 error / 41.68 unset); checkout's other operations (oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart, oteldemo.CheckoutService/prepareOrderItems, oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, oteldemo.CurrencyService/Convert, oteldemo.ShippingService/GetQuote, oteldemo.ShippingService/ShipOrder) had zero error spans.","evidence_ids":["919ff1cf-20cf-4974-b778-49c01427b1c7-t0:b3968366-3412-4ad4-bd05-12e658560781","a4914fe8-d639-4ef9-8235-fee990140d18-t0:25e012d7-7514-4197-8601-61adef15aae6"],"target_refs":["m0-otel-20260909"],"time_scope_ref":"policy-window-1"},{"kind":"fact","text":"Payment's own server span grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge recorded 57.95 STATUS_CODE_ERROR over the same hour (the only payment operations present were charge, ResolveFloat and grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge, with errors only on the Charge server span).","evidence_ids":["2dfaf6c3-5ea0-4fcc-8a91-922ab916267b-t0:03e050c9-2584-4b2d-8642-1d36883e2c9f"],"target_refs":["m0-otel-20260909"],"time_scope_ref":"policy-window-1"},{"kind":"fact","text":"The exact error raised in payment is 'Payment request failed. incident.acceptance_step: eval-suite development baseline (not an acceptance step)

stimulus.question: Checkout is reported to show elevated errors in the OTel Demo. Using the authorized metrics range query and trace search for the last 5 minutes, determine whether checkout and its dependency calls (payment, product-catalog, cart, currency, shipping, email) show failures or elevated latency, cite trace ids, and return a json investigation report.

claims.text: In the 61 minutes ending 2026-11-03T19:23:13Z, checkout's oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder spans split into 58.97 STATUS_CODE_ERROR and 41.68 STATUS_CODE_UNSET, and checkout's client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge had the identical counts (58.97 error / 41.68 unset); checkout's other operations (oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart, oteldemo.CheckoutService/prepareOrderItems, oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, oteldemo.CurrencyService/Convert, oteldemo.ShippingService/GetQuote, oteldemo.ShippingService/ShipOrder) had zero error spans.

Payment's own server span grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge recorded 57.95 STATUS_CODE_ERROR over the same hour (the only payment operations present were charge, ResolveFloat and grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge, with errors only on the Charge server span).

The exact error raised in payment is 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. app.loyalty.level=gold' (tags grpc.error_name=Error, grpc.error_message, plus exception.message/exception.stacktrace), and the stack trace names payment's own code: 'at module.exports.charge (/usr/src/app/charge.js:37:13)' via 'async Object.chargeServiceHandler [as charge] (/usr/src/app/index.js:21:22)'.

Checkout's errored PlaceOrder spans carry rpc.grpc.status_code=13 with otel.status_description 'failed to charge card: could not charge the card: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = Payment request failed. Invalid token. app.loyalty.level=gold', i.e. the failure is reported by checkout as a propagated payment RPC error, not a checkout-local fault.

Visible failure traces propagate the same cause outward: frontend spans 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout', 'POST /api/checkout' and client 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' carry http.status_code 500 with exception message '13 INTERNAL: failed to charge card: ... Payment request failed. Invalid token. app.loyalty.level=gold'; over the hour frontend POST /api/checkout and grpc PlaceOrder client spans each had 57.95 error spans, frontend-proxy ingress and 'router frontend egress' 58.97 each, and load-generator POST 58.97.

The 5-minute PlaceOrder error ratio was exactly 1 at 19:17:13 and 19:18:13, then 0.5 at 19:19:13, 0.25 at 19:20:13, and 0 at 19:21:13 and 19:22:13; payment's 5-minute Charge error ratio was 1 at 19:17:13 and 19:18:13, 0.5 at 19:19:13, 0.25 at 19:20:13 and 19:21:13, 0 at 19:22:13 and 19:23:13. This reproduces the alert annotation's 100% figure shortly before the 2026-11-03T19:22:13Z alert start.

A 24h baseline shows PlaceOrder error counts of 0 for the hours from 2026-11-02T20:23Z through 2026-11-03T11:53Z, with the first non-zero hours around 2026-11-03T12:23Z (8.14), 12:53Z (29.49) and 13:23Z (30.51), and the most recent hour showing 60 error vs 41.69 unset spans; payment's Charge series follows the same shape.

PlaceOrder volume is very low and bursty, so the ratio is volatile: in 2-minute windows between 18:24:13Z and 19:23:13Z totals per window ranged from 0 to about 12 spans, with windows of pure error (e.g. 19:15:13 with 10 error and 0 unset) adjacent to windows of pure success.

Payment's failing Charge span evaluated a flag via flagd: trace 15c58e0d253267e7bfe60f3a6faf15a4 contains a child span grpc.flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveFloat (rpc.grpc.status_code 0) under the errored payment server span. Over the hour payment's ResolveFloat client spans totalled 10.17 with no error status, and flagd's own ResolveFloat spans totalled 126.07 with no error status.

No restarts or redeploys of either pod are visible: kube_pod_container_info for payment-6f7bc865d6-bfxbv (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo@sha256:33f327b357617379bfa3b292f430d1f06e66e2872494125a40bae14d8fe57d87) and for checkout-c676dc885-7h9mn were continuously 1 across 24h, and the kube_replicaset_owner series for the payment and checkout deployments (12+ series, including payment-6f7bc865d6 and payment-7bd449ddbf) were present with value 1 at every 30-minute step of the window, i.e. no new ReplicaSet series appeared. app_payment_transactions_total is sourced from the single pod payment-6f7bc865d6-bfxbv throughout.

The only other error spans in the hour belong to flagd self/streaming operations, not to checkout's call path: flagd 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' 8.13 error spans, ad 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' 6.1, recommendation '/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' 6.1, while ad's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, frontend's GET /api/data, /api/products/[productId], /api/recommendations, grpc AdService/GetAds, grpc ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, cart's POST /oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart and product-catalog's oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct all had 0 error spans. No evidence ties these EventStream errors to the PlaceOrder failures.

Fast, immediate application rejection rather than slowness: errored payment Charge spans completed in 428-5867 microseconds with an exception stack trace from charge.js, and successful charges during the same period completed in 504-5862 microseconds, so there is no timeout or saturation signature in the failing calls.

Rejected: a payment pod crash, restart or redeploy at incident time. Payment and checkout pods show a single continuous container record with unchanged image digests for the whole 24h window and no new ReplicaSet series appears, while the failure is an application exception thrown from payment's own charge.js.

Rejected: a fault inside checkout's own order assembly or its other dependencies. checkout's prepareOrderItems had 0 error spans, and its calls to cart (GetCart 100.65 unset, EmptyCart 41.68 unset), product-catalog (GetProduct 184.02 unset), currency (Convert 284.67 unset) and shipping (GetQuote 100.65 unset, ShipOrder 41.68 unset) all recorded 0 error spans, while every errored PlaceOrder maps 1:1 to an errored Charge call.

Primary hypothesis for the deepest cause: payment's charge handler is executing a configured failure path (a flagd-evaluated fault/percentage switch) that rejects charges for sessions carrying loyalty level 'gold', producing the 'Invalid token' error. Support: the thrown message embeds app.loyalty.level=gold, a flagd ResolveFloat evaluation is a child of the failing Charge span, and payment's error rate is a partial, time-varying fraction rather than a total outage. The flag key, its variant/value and when it changed are not exposed by any available metric, so this remains a hypothesis.

Secondary hypothesis: the failures are restricted to gold-loyalty checkout sessions. Every observed payment error message ends with 'app.loyalty.level=gold', but successful Charge spans expose no loyalty attribute, so the loyalty mix of successful charges and therefore the cohort restriction cannot be confirmed from this evidence.

gaps: The alert's own expression/recording rule checkout_placeorder_error_ratio is not present in the queried Prometheus: get_metric_names with {__name__=~"checkout.*|.*error_ratio.*|.*placeorder.*"} returned no metric names, so the alert's exact definition, window and evaluation instants could not be verified; the 100% annotation was only reproduced by computing a 5-minute PlaceOrder error ratio (1.0 at 19:17:13 and 19:18:13), and the ratio was already 0 at 19:21:13 and 19:22:13.

No flagd flag-level metric exists to show which flag or variant changed and when (get_metric_names {__name__=~"flagd.*"} returned no names), and flagd configuration/audit state is not among the available sources.

change_history and pod_logs integrations are listed as not_integrated, so the change that introduced the payment charge rejections around 2026-11-03T12:23Z cannot be identified, and payment container logs for the charge.js:37 throw could not be read.
No loyalty-level labelled metric exists (get_metric_names {__name__=~".*loyalty.*"} returned no names), so the loyalty mix of successful versus failed charges is unknown.

rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_count{service_name="payment"} returned no data, so payment's server-side latency and gRPC status distribution could not be cross-checked independently of span metrics.

Currency, shipping, email, accounting, fraud-detection, quote, image-provider and kafka own error signals were not queried directly; only their absence in the error-span breakdown (no error series returned) and checkout's zero-error client spans to currency/shipping are known.

No container CPU/memory or node resource metrics were examined, so resource pressure as a contributing factor in payment cannot be positively excluded, although the failing calls are immediate application exceptions, not timeouts.
next_steps: Inspect the flagd flag configuration (and its change/audit history) for a payment charge-failure flag and confirm whether its variant or targeting changed around 2026-11-03T12:23Z.
Read payment container logs around 2026-11-03T12:23Z for the charge.js:37 'Invalid token' throw, including the loyalty-level values of requests that were rejected.

Retrieve the alerting rule definition for checkout_placeorder_error_ratio to confirm its window and threshold, and consider whether a 5-minute ratio over such a low PlaceOrder volume needs a minimum-request-count guard.
Confirm whether only gold-loyalty sessions were rejected by comparing loyalty level on successful versus failed charge requests (requires request attributes or logs, not available in this Run).
report_parsed.summary: Checkout is firing CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh because the payment service is rejecting card charges with an application-level error thrown inside payment itself: 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. app.loyalty.level=gold' (thrown at payment's /usr/src/app/charge.js:37). Checkout propagates that as gRPC status 13 INTERNAL on oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, and frontend/frontend-proxy/load-generator observe HTTP 500. In the hour ending 2026-11-03T19:23:13Z, 58.97 of checkout's PlaceOrder spans carried STATUS_CODE_ERROR versus 41.68 UNSET (~59%), exactly mirroring the 58.97 errors on checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge client spans and payment's own 57.95 errored grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge server spans. The 5-minute PlaceOrder error ratio was 1.0 at 19:17:13 and 19:18:13, which reproduces the alert annotation's '100% over the last 5 minutes'; the ratio then fell to 0.5/0.25 and to 0 at 19:21:13-19:22:13, so the firing reflects very low, bursty PlaceOrder volume. A comparable 24h baseline shows zero PlaceOrder error spans for ~10 consecutive hours (2026-11-02T20:23Z through 2026-11-03T11:53Z), with errors first appearing around 12:23Z and escalating. Nothing in the evidence shows a pod restart or redeploy of payment or checkout (same pod UIDs and same image digests for 24h), and every other checkout dependency (cart, product-catalog, currency, shipping) had zero error spans; the deepest supported cause is payment's own charge-rejection logic, and what turned it on is not observable with the available sources.
